items.html:
Oil, gas & LNG
🇻🇪 Venezuela’s Oil Exports Drop 9% as Freight Costs Bite
oilprice.com
Venezuela’s oil exports fell nearly 9% in September to 1.08 million barrels per day as soaring tanker costs forced traders to demand steeper discounts and delayed cargoes leaving the country.
What it means: Less is moving from this origin: crude, LNG and product buyers can expect firmer offers and longer lead times for a few weeks.

Shipping, ports & logistics  Panama Canal
🇵🇦 New limits: More ships can transit this key cargo chokepoint
freightwaves.com
The Panama Canal has raised the number of daily transit slots for the largest container vessels.
What it means: The Panama Canal carries Atlantic → Pacific (US Gulf LNG & grain → Asia) and logged 1 critical signal this week. More capacity on this route: shippers and forwarders can expect shorter queues and softer slot premiums, usually within weeks.

Oil, gas & LNG  Strait of Hormuz
🇮🇷 Middle East Oil Exports Stage a Remarkable Comeback
oilprice.com · 2 reports this week
Exports of crude oil from the Middle East hit their highest level in September since the war with Iran began, reinforcing a trend of increased supplies despite Iranian attacks on shipping in the…
What it means: The Strait of Hormuz carries Gulf crude, LNG & products → Asia and logged 5 critical signals this week. More is moving from this origin: crude, LNG and product buyers get more offers and softer premiums; freight on the route tends to follow.

Shipping, ports & logistics  Strait of Hormuz
🇮🇷 Crude oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz hit prewar levels, but fuel shipments remain constrained
hellenicshippingnews.com · 6 reports this week
Crude oil exports from the Strait of Hormuz have basically returned to levels normal before the Iran war, as U.S. military escorts have boosted shipments and pipelines have redirected flows.
What it means: The Strait of Hormuz carries Gulf crude, LNG & products → Asia and logged 5 critical signals this week. More capacity on this route: shippers and forwarders can expect shorter queues and softer slot premiums, usually within weeks.

Agriculture & food
🇨🇳 Wheat bounces and corn manages a mostly firm finish
brownfieldagnews.com
Soybeans were lower on fund and technical selling. Export sales were up on the week at 38 million bushels, led by China, but the Golden Week holiday could limit their demand for a few days.
What it means: Less is moving from this origin: grain and food importers can expect firmer offers and longer lead times for a few weeks.
